english_source:
5590 — Kab ibn Malik was demanding a debt owed to him by Ibn Abi Hadrad in the mosque, and their voices rose until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard them while he was in his house. He came out to them and lifted the curtain of his room, then called: “O Kab.” He said: “At your service, O Messenger of Allah ﷺ.” He said: “Reduce some of your debt,” indicating half of it. Kab said: “I have done so, O Messenger of Allah ﷺ.” He then said: “Get up and pay him.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (457) and Muslim (1558).

٥٥٩١ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( الصلح جائز بين المسلمين )).

حسن: رواه أبو داود (٣٥٩٤).

قال أبو داود: زاد أحمد بن عبد الوهاب: (( إلا صلحًا أحل حرامًا، أو حرَّم حلالًا )).

english_source:
5591 — Abu Hurairah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Settlement is permissible among Muslims.”

Hasan: Narrated by Abu Dawud (3594).

Abu Dawud said: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Wahhab added: “Except a settlement that makes the unlawful lawful or makes the lawful unlawful.”

٥٥٩٢ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( اشترى رجل من رجل عقارًا له، فوجد الرجل الذي اشترى العقار في عقاره جرة فيها ذهب، فقال له الذي اشترى العقار: خذ ذهبك مني، إنما اشتريت منك الأرض، ولم أبتع منك الذهب. فقال الذي شرى الأرض: إنما بعتك الأرض وما فيها. فتحاكما إلى رجل، فقال الذي تحاكما إليه: ألكما ولد؟ قال أحدهما: لي غلام. وقال الآخر: لي جارية. قال: أنكحوا الغلام الجارية، وأنفقوا على أنفسكما منه، وتصدقا )).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٤٧٢)، ومسلم (١٧٢١).

5592 — Abu Hurairah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “A man bought a piece of land from another man, then the buyer found in that land a jar containing gold. The buyer said to the seller: ‘Take your gold from me. I only bought the land from you, I did not buy the gold.’ The seller said: ‘I sold you the land and whatever was in it.’ So they brought their case to a man for judgment. He asked them: ‘Do either of you have children?’ One of them said: ‘I have a boy.’ The other said: ‘I have a girl.’ He said: ‘Marry the boy to the girl, spend from it on yourselves, and give charity.’”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3472) and Muslim (1721).

٥٥٩٣ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن الزبير أن رجلًا من الأنصار خاصم الزبير عند رسول اللّٰه ﷺ في شراج الحرة التي يسقون بها النخل، فقال الأنصاري: سرح الماء يمر، فأبى عليه، فاختصما عند النبي ﷺ، فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( اسق يا زبير، ثم أرسل الماء إلى جارك )). فغضب الأنصاري، فقال: أن كان ابن عمتك. فتلون وجه رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، ثم قال: (( اسق يا زبير، ثم احبس الماء حتى يرجع إلى الجدر )). فقال الزبير: والله إن لأحسب هذه الآية نزلت في ذلك: ( فَلَا وَرَبِّكَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ حَتَّىٰ يُحَكِّمُوكَ فِيمَا شَجَرَ بَيْنَهُمْ ) [سورة النساء: ٦٥].

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٣٦٠ ،٢٣٥٩)، ومسلم (٢٣٥٧).

5593 — Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr narrated that a man from the Ansar disputed with al-Zubayr before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ over the irrigation channels of al-Harrah from which they watered the palm trees. The Ansari said: “Let the water pass through.” But al-Zubayr refused. So they brought their dispute to the Prophet ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Water your land, O Zubayr, then let the water pass to your neighbor.” The Ansari became angry and said: “Because he is your aunt’s son?” The face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ changed color, then he said: “Water your land, O Zubayr, then hold back the water until it returns to the boundary wall.” Al-Zubayr said: By Allah, I believe this verse was revealed concerning that: “But no, by your Lord, they do not truly believe until they make you judge concerning what has arisen between them.” [al-Nisa: 65]

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2359, 2360) and Muslim (2357).

٥٥٩٤ — عن الزبير:

أنه خاصم رجلًا من الأنصار قد شهد بدرًا إلى رسول الله ﷺ في شراج من الحرة، كانا يسقيان به كلاهما.

فقال رسول الله ﷺ للزبير:

«اسْقِ يَا زُبَيْرُ، ثُمَّ أَرْسِلْ إِلَى جَارِكَ».

فغضب الأنصاري، فقال:

يا رسول الله، أن كان ابن عمتك؟

فتلون وجه رسول الله ﷺ، ثم قال:

«اسْقِ، ثُمَّ احْبِسْ حَتَّى يَبْلُغَ الْجَدْرَ».

فاستوعى رسول الله ﷺ حينئذ حقه للزبير، وكان رسول الله ﷺ قبل ذلك أشار على الزبير برأي سعة له وللأنصاري، فلما أحفظ الأنصاري رسول الله ﷺ استوعى للزبير حقه في صريح الحكم.

قال عروة: قال الزبير:

والله ما أحسب هذه الآية نزلت إلا في ذلك:

{فَلَا وَرَبِّكَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ حَتَّىٰ يُحَكِّمُوكَ فِيمَا شَجَرَ بَيْنَهُمْ}.

صحيح: رواه البخاري (٢٧٠٨).

وقوله: «فلما أحفظ» أي: أغضب.

english_source:
5594 — Al-Zubayr reported:

He disputed with a man from the Anṣār who had participated in Badr, and they brought their dispute before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning an irrigation channel in al-Ḥarrah from which both of them watered their land.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to al-Zubayr:

“Water your land, O Zubayr, then let the water pass on to your neighbor.”

The Anṣārī became angry and said:

“O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, is it because he is your aunt’s son?”

The face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ changed color. Then he said:

“Water your land, then hold back the water until it reaches the boundary wall.”

At that point, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ granted al-Zubayr his full legal right. Before that, he had advised al-Zubayr to follow a lenient arrangement that would accommodate both him and the Anṣārī. But when the Anṣārī angered the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he granted al-Zubayr his full right according to the explicit judgment.

ʿUrwah said that al-Zubayr said:

“By Allah, I think this verse was revealed concerning this incident:

‘But no, by your Lord, they will not truly believe until they make you judge concerning what has arisen between them.’”

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (2708).

The expression “when he angered him” means when he provoked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to anger.

٥٥٩٥ — عن عائشة أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ كان يدعو في الصلاة، ويقول: (( اللهم إني أعوذ بك من المأثم والمغرم )). فقال له قائل: ما أكثر ما تستعيذ - يا رسول الله - من المغرم! قال: (( إن الرجل إذا غرم حدث فكذب، ووعد فأخلف )).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٣٩٧)، ومسلم (٥٨٩). واللفظ للبخاري.

5595 — Aishah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to supplicate in prayer and say: “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from sin and debt.” Someone said to him: “How often you seek refuge, O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, from debt.” He said: “When a man falls into debt, he speaks and lies, and he promises and breaks his promise.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2397) and Muslim (589). The wording is al-Bukhari’s.

٥٥٩٦ — عن ابن عمر قال: سمعت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يقول: (( من حالت شفاعته دون حد من حدود الله عز وجل فقد ضاد الله في أمره. ومن مات وعليه دين فليس بالدينار ولا بالدرهم، ولكنها الحسنات والسيئات. ومن خاصم في باطل - وهو يعلمه - لم يزل في سخط الله حتى ينزع. ومن قال في مؤمن ما ليس فيه أسكنه الله ردغة الخبال حتى يخرج مما قال )).

صحيح: رواه الإمام أحمد (٥٣٨٥)، وصححه الحاكم (٢٧/٢)، والبيهقي (٨٢/٦).

وقوله: (( أسكنه الله في ردغة الخبال )) الردغة طين ووحل كثير، جمعه ردغ ورداغ.

والخبال في الأصل الفساد، ويكون في الأفعال، والأبدان، والعقول. وقد ورد تفسيره في الحديث أنه عصارة أهل النار.

5596 — Ibn Umar said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever intercedes to prevent one of the prescribed punishments of Allah has opposed Allah in His command. Whoever dies while owing a debt, then repayment there will not be in gold coins or silver coins, but rather in good deeds and bad deeds. Whoever argues for falsehood while knowing it remains under the anger of Allah until he stops. And whoever says about a believer what is not true, Allah will make him dwell in the foul mire until he comes out of what he said.”

Authentic: Narrated by Ahmad (5385), authenticated by al-Hakim (2/27), and by al-Bayhaqi (6/82).

The phrase “Allah will make him dwell in the foul mire” means thick mud and filth.

The word refers originally to corruption and ruin, whether in actions, bodies, or minds. It has also been explained in hadith as the discharge of the people of Hell.

٥٥٩٦ — عن ابن عمر قال: سمعت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يقول: (( من حالت شفاعته دون حد من حدود الله عز وجل فقد ضاد الله في أمره. ومن مات وعليه دين فليس بالدينار ولا بالدرهم، ولكنها الحسنات والسيئات. ومن خاصم في باطل - وهو يعلمه - لم يزل في سخط الله حتى ينزع. ومن قال في مؤمن ما ليس فيه أسكنه الله ردغة الخبال حتى يخرج مما قال )).

صحيح: رواه الإمام أحمد (٥٣٨٥)، وصححه الحاكم (٢٧/٢)، والبيهقي (٨٢/٦).

وقوله: (( أسكنه الله في ردغة الخبال )) الردغة طين ووحل كثير، جمعه ردغ ورداغ.

Whoever argues for falsehood while knowing it remains under the anger of Allah until he stops. And whoever says about a believer what is not true, Allah will make him dwell in the foul mire until he comes out of what he said.”

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1885).

٥٦٠٣ — عن جابر أنه أخبره أن أباه توفي وترك عليه ثلاثين وسقًا لرجل من اليهود، فاستنظره جابر، فأبى أن ينظره، فكلم جابر رسول اللّٰه ﷺ؛ ليشفع له إليه، فجاء رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فكلم اليهودي ليأخذ ثمر نخله بالذي له، فأبى، فدخل رسول اللّٰه ﷺ النخل، فمشى فيها، ثم قال لجابر: (( جُدَّ له، فأوفِ له الذي له )). فجده بعدما رجع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فأوفاه ثلاثين وسقًا، وفضلت له سبعة عشر وسقًا، فجاء جابر رسول اللّٰه ﷺ ليخبره بالذي كان، فوجده يصلي العصر، فلما انصرف أخبره بالفضل، فقال: (( أخبر ذلك ابن الخطاب )). فذهب جابر إلى عمر، فأخبره، فقال له عمر: لقد علمت حين مشى فيها رسول اللّٰه ﷺ ليباركن فيها.

صحيح: رواه البخاري (٢٣٩٦).

5603 — Jabir narrated that his father died and left behind a debt of thirty wasqs owed to a Jewish man. Jabir asked him to grant time, but he refused. So Jabir spoke to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to intercede for him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and spoke to the Jew so that he would take the produce of his palm trees for what was owed to him, but he refused. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the orchard and walked through it, then said to Jabir: “Harvest it and pay him what is owed to him.” So Jabir harvested it after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned, paid him the thirty wasqs, and seventeen wasqs remained extra. Jabir came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to tell him what had happened and found him praying Asr. When he finished, Jabir told him about the surplus, and he said: “Inform Ibn al-Khattab of that.” Jabir went to Umar and informed him, and Umar said to him: I knew when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ walked through it that blessing would be placed in it.

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2396).

٥٦٠٤ — عن سعد بن الأطول أن أخاه مات، وترك ثلاثمائة درهم، وترك عيالًا، فأردت أن أنفقها على عياله. فقال النبي ﷺ: (( إن أخاك محتبس بدينه، فاقض عنه )). فقال: يا رسول الله، قد أديت عنه إلا دينارين ادعتهما امرأة، وليس لها بينة. قال: (( فأعطها فإنها محقة )).

حسن: رواه ابن ماجه (٢٤٣٣)، وأحمد (٢٠٠٧٧ ،٢٠٠٧٦ ،١٧٢٢٧).

5604 — Sad ibn al-Atwal said that his brother died and left three hundred dirhams and left dependents behind. I wanted to spend that money on his dependents. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Your brother is being held back by his debt, so pay it off for him.” He said: “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I have paid it except for two dinars that a woman claims, but she has no proof.” He said: “Give them to her, for she is truthful.”

Hasan: Narrated by Ibn Majah (2433) and Ahmad (20077, 20076, 17227).

٥٦٠٥ — عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي ﷺ قال: (( لو كان عندي أُحُد ذهبًا لأحببت أن لا يأتي عليَّ ثلاث، وعندي منه دينار - ليس شيء أرصده في دين علي - أجد من يقبله )).

5605 — Abu Hurairah narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: “If I had Uhud mountain in gold, I would not like three nights to pass while a single dinar remained with me — except something I set aside for a debt upon me — until I found someone to take it.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (7228) and Muslim (991).

The phrase “I set aside” means: I reserve it.

5606 — Abu Dharr said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “It would not please me to have the like of this mountain of Uhud in gold and for three nights to pass while I still had a dinar of it, except something I reserve for a debt, unless I were to distribute it among the servants of Allah like this, and this, and this,” to his right, to his left, and behind him.

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (6444) and Muslim (992).

5609 — Abdullah ibn Jafar said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Allah is with the debtor until he pays his debt, so long as it was not incurred in something Allah dislikes.”

Hasan: Narrated by Ibn Majah (2409), al-Darimi (2637), al-Hakim (2/23), and al-Bayhaqi (5/355).

٥٦١٠ — عن أبي هريرة أن رجلًا أتى النبي ﷺ يتقاضاه بعيرًا، قال: فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( أعطوه )). فقالوا: لا نجد إلا سنًّا أفضل من سنه. فقال الرجل: أوفيتني أوفاك الله. فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( أعطوه؛ فإن من خيار الناس أحسنهم قضاءً )).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٣٩٢)، ومسلم (١٢٢ :١٦٠١). واللفظ للبخاري.

5610 — Abu Hurairah narrated that a man came to the Prophet ﷺ demanding a camel that he was owed. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Give it to him.” They said: “We only find one better in age than his.” The man said: “You have fulfilled my due — may Allah fulfill yours.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Give it to him, for the best of people are those best in repayment.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2392) and Muslim (1601:122). The wording is al-Bukhari’s.

٥٦١١ — عن أبي هريرة قال: كان لرجل على رسول اللّٰه ﷺ حق، فأغلظ له، فهمَّ به أصحاب النبي ﷺ، فقال النبي ﷺ: (( إن لصاحب الحق مقالًا، اشتروا له سنًّا فأعطوه إياه )). فقالوا: إنا لا نجد إلا سنًّا هو خير من سنه. قال: (( فاشتروا فأعطوه إياه؛ فإن من خيركم - أو خيركم - أحسنكم قضاءً )).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٣٠٦)، ومسلم (١٢٠ :١٦٠١). واللفظ لمسلم.

وعند البخاري في أوله: (( دعوه؛ فإن لصاحب الحق مقالًا … )).

5611 — Abu Hurairah said: A man had a claim against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he spoke harshly to him. The companions of the Prophet ﷺ intended to deal with him, but the Prophet ﷺ said: “The one who has a right may speak. Buy for him a camel of the proper age and give it to him.” They said: “We only find one better than his.” He said: “Then buy it and give it to him, for among the best of you — or the best of you — are those best in repayment.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2306) and Muslim (1601:120). The wording is Muslim’s.

In al-Bukhari the beginning reads: “Leave him, for the one who has a right may speak.”

٥٦١٢ — عن أبي هريرة قال:

أتى النبي ﷺ رجل يتقاضاه، قد استسلف منه شطر وسق، فأعطاه وسقًا، فقال:

«نِصْفُ وَسْقٍ لَكَ، وَنِصْفُ وَسْقٍ لَكَ مِنْ عِنْدِي».

ثم جاء صاحب الوسق يتقاضاه، فأعطاه وسقين، فقال رسول الله ﷺ:

«وَسْقٌ لَكَ، وَوَسْقٌ مِنْ عِنْدِي».

حسن: رواه البزار في كشف الأستار (١٣٠٦).

5612 — Abū Hurayrah reported:

A man came to the Prophet ﷺ seeking repayment of half a wasq that the Prophet ﷺ had borrowed from him. He gave him a full wasq and said:

“Half a wasq is what is due to you, and the other half wasq is a gift from me.”

Then another man to whom a full wasq was owed came seeking repayment. The Prophet ﷺ gave him two wasqs and said:

“One wasq is what is due to you, and one wasq is from me.”

Hasan: Narrated by al-Bazzār in Kashf al-Astār (1306).

«نِصْفُ وَسْقٍ لَكَ، وَنِصْفُ وَسْقٍ لَكَ مِنْ عِنْدِي».

ثم جاء صاحب الوسق يتقاضاه، فأعطاه وسقين، فقال رسول الله ﷺ:

«وَسْقٌ لَكَ، وَوَسْقٌ مِنْ عِنْدِي».

حسن: رواه البزار في كشف الأستار (١٣٠٦).

5612 — Abū Hurayrah reported:

A man came to the Prophet ﷺ seeking repayment of half a wasq that the Prophet ﷺ had borrowed from him. He gave him a full wasq and said:

“Half a wasq is what is due to you, and the other half wasq is a gift from me.”

Then another man to whom a full wasq was owed came seeking repayment. The Prophet ﷺ gave him two wasqs and said:

“One wasq is what is due to you, and one wasq is from me.”

Hasan: Narrated by al-Bazzār in Kashf al-Astār (1306).

٥٦١٣ — عن أبي رافع مولى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ أنه قال: استسلف رسول اللّٰه ﷺ بكرًا فجاءته إبل من الصدقة. قال أبو رافع: فأمرني رسول اللّٰه ﷺ أن أقضي الرجل بكره، فقلت: لم أجد في الإبل إلا جملا خيارًا رباعيًّا، فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( أعطه إياه؛ فإن خيار الناس أحسنهم قضاءً )).

صحيح: رواه مالك (٨٩)، ومسلم (١١٨ :١٦٠٠).

قال مالك: “لا بأس بأن يقبض من أسلف شيئًا من الذهب أو الورق أو الطعام أو الحيوان ممن أسلفه ذلك أفضل مما أسلفه إذا لم يكن ذلك على شرط منهما أو عادة، فإن كان ذلك على شرط أو وعد أو عادة فذلك مكروه، ولا خير فيه”.

وقوله: (( أو وعد )) أي وعد سابق.

english_source:
5613 — Abu Rafi, the freed slave of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ borrowed a young camel. Then camels from charity arrived. Abu Rafi said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered me to repay the man his camel. I said: “I found among the camels only an excellent mature camel.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Give it to him, for the best of people are those best in repayment.”

Authentic: Narrated by Malik (89) and Muslim (1600:118).

Malik said: There is no harm in a person receiving, from one to whom he loaned gold, silver, food, or animals, something better than what he loaned, so long as it was not stipulated between them and was not a customary expectation. If it was a condition, a promise, or an established habit, then it is disliked and not good.

The word “or a promise” means: a prior promise.

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2394) and Muslim (715:71). The wording is Muslim’s.

٥٦١٥ — عن إسماعيل بن إبراهيم بن عبد اللّٰه بن أبي ربيعة المخزومي، عن أبيه، عن جده أن النبي ﷺ استسلف منه حين غزا حنين ثلاثين أو أربعين ألفًا، فلما قدم قضاها إياه. ثم قال له النبي ﷺ: (( بارك اللّٰه لك في أهلك ومالك. إنما جزاء السلف الوفاء والحمد )).

حسن: رواه النسائي (٤٦٨٣)، وابن ماجه (٢٤٢٤)، وأحمد (١٦٤١٠)، والبيهقي (٣٥٥/٥).

english_source:
5615 — Ismail ibn Ibrahim ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Rabiah al-Makhzumi narrated from his father, from his grandfather, that the Prophet ﷺ borrowed from him thirty or forty thousand during the campaign of Hunayn. When he returned, he repaid him. Then the Prophet ﷺ said to him: “May Allah bless your family and your wealth. The reward for a loan is repayment and gratitude.”

Hasan: Narrated by al-Nasai (4683), Ibn Majah (2424), Ahmad (16410), and al-Bayhaqi (5/355).

Hasan: Narrated by al-Nasai (4619), Ibn Majah (2286), Ahmad (17149), al-Hakim (2/30), and al-Bayhaqi (5/351).

٥٦١٧ — عن عائشة قالت:

ابتاع رسول الله ﷺ من رجل من الأعراب جزورًا - أو جزائر - بوسق من تمر الذخرة، وتمر الذخرة العجوة.

فرجع به رسول الله ﷺ إلى بيته، فالتمس له التمر فلم يجده، فخرج إليه رسول الله ﷺ فقال له:

«يَا عَبْدَ اللَّهِ، إِنَّا قَدِ ابْتَعْنَا مِنْكَ جَزُورًا - أَوْ جَزَائِرَ - بِوَسْقٍ مِنْ تَمْرِ الذَّخِرَةِ، فَالْتَمَسْنَاهُ فَلَمْ نَجِدْهُ».

فقال الأعرابي:

واغدراه!

قالت: فنهمه الناس وقالوا:

قاتلك الله، أيغدر رسول الله ﷺ؟

5617 — ʿĀʾishah reported:

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ purchased from a Bedouin a camel—or several camels—for one wasq of al-dhakhīrah dates, and al-dhakhīrah dates were ʿajwah dates.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned home with the animal and searched for the dates to pay the man, but he could not find them. He went out to the Bedouin and said:

“O servant of Allah, we purchased from you a camel—or camels—for one wasq of al-dhakhīrah dates, but we looked for them and could not find them.”

The Bedouin exclaimed:

“What treachery!”

The people rebuked him and said:

“May Allah deal with you! Would the Messenger of Allah ﷺ betray anyone?”

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

“Leave him, for the person who possesses a right is entitled to speak.”

Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ repeated to him:

“O servant of Allah, we purchased your camels while thinking that we possessed what we had specified for you. We searched for it, but we could not find it.”

The Bedouin again exclaimed:

“What treachery!”

The people rebuked him and said:

“May Allah deal with you! Would the Messenger of Allah ﷺ betray anyone?”

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

“Leave him, for the person who possesses a right is entitled to speak.”

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ repeated this two or three times.

When he saw that the man did not understand, he said to one of his Companions:

“Go to Khuwaylah bint Ḥakīm ibn Umayyah and say to her: ‘The Messenger of Allah ﷺ says to you: If you have one wasq of al-dhakhīrah dates, lend it to us until we repay you, if Allah wills.’”

The man went to her and then returned, saying:

“She says: Yes, I have it, O Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Send someone to collect it.”

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the man:

“Take it to him and give him in full what is owed to him.”

So he took it and paid the Bedouin his full due.

ʿĀʾishah said:

The Bedouin later passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was sitting among his Companions and said:

“May Allah reward you with good. You have paid in full and dealt generously.”

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

“Those are the best servants of Allah in the sight of Allah on the Day of Resurrection: those who fulfill what they owe and do so graciously.”

Hasan: Narrated by Aḥmad (26312) and al-Bazzār in Kashf al-Astār (1309).

“Those are the best servants of Allah in the sight of Allah on the Day of Resurrection: those who fulfill what they owe and do so graciously.”

Hasan: Narrated by Aḥmad (26312) and al-Bazzār in Kashf al-Astār (1309).

٥٦٢٠ — عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:

«مَطْلُ الْغَنِيِّ ظُلْمٌ، وَإِذَا أُتْبِعَ أَحَدُكُمْ عَلَى مَلِيءٍ فَلْيَتَّبِعْ».

متفق عليه: رواه مالك (٨٤)، والبخاري (٢٢٨٧)، ومسلم (١٥٦٤).

“Delay in payment by one who is able to pay is injustice. If one of you is referred for payment to a solvent person, then let him accept the transfer.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by Mālik (84), al-Bukhārī (2287), and Muslim (1564).

٥٦٢١ — عن جابر بن عبد اللّٰه أن أباه قتل يوم أحد شهيدًا وعليه دين، فاشتد الغرماء في حقوقهم، فأتيت النبي ﷺ، فسألهم أن يقبلوا تمر حائطي، ويحللوا أبي، فأبوا، فلم يعطهم النبي ﷺ حائطي، وقال: (( سنغدو عليك )). فغدا علينا حين أصبح، فطاف في النخل، ودعا في ثمرها بالبركة، فجددتها فقضيتهم، وبقي لنا من تمرها.

صحيح: رواه البخاري (٢٣٩٥).

صحيح: رواه البخاري (٢٣٩٥).
english_source:
5621 — Jabir ibn Abdullah said: My father was killed as a martyr on the Day of Uhud and he had debts. The creditors pressed strongly for their rights, so I came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him to request that they accept the dates of my orchard and release my father, but they refused. The Prophet ﷺ did not hand over my orchard to them and said: “We will come to you in the morning.” So he came to us in the morning, walked through the palm trees, and supplicated for blessing in their fruit. Then I harvested the dates, repaid the creditors, and some of the dates remained for us.

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2395).

٥٦٢٢ — عن جابر بن عبد اللّٰه قال: غزوت مع النبي ﷺ، فقال: (( كيف ترى بعيرك؟ أتبيعه؟ )) قلت: نعم، فبعته إياه، فلما قدم المدينة غدوت إليه بالبعير، فأعطاني ثمنه.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٣٨٥)، ومسلم (١١ :٧١٥) واللفظ للبخاري.

5622 — Jabir ibn Abdullah said: I went on a campaign with the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: “How do you find your camel? Will you sell it?” I said: Yes. So I sold it to him. When we arrived in Madinah, I brought the camel to him in the morning, and he gave me its price.

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2385) and Muslim (715:11). The wording is al-Bukhari’s.

٥٦٢٣ — عن أبي هريرة، عن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ أنه ذكر: (( أن رجلا من بني إسرائيل سأل بعض بني إسرائيل أن يسلفه ألف دينار، قال: ائتني بشهداء أشهدهم. قال: كفى بالله شهيدا. قال: ائتني بالكفيل. قال: كفى بالله كفيلا. قال: صدقت. فدفعها إليه إلى أجل مسمى )). الحديث.

صحيح: رواه أحمد (٨٥٨٧) والبخاري (٢٤٠٤) تعليقا.

5623 — Abu Hurairah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned: “A man from the Children of Israel asked another man from the Children of Israel to lend him one thousand dinars. He said: ‘Bring me witnesses so I may have them witness it.’ He said: ‘Allah is sufficient as a witness.’ He said: ‘Bring me a guarantor.’ He said: ‘Allah is sufficient as a guarantor.’ He said: ‘You have spoken truthfully.’ So he gave it to him until a specified term.” The rest of the hadith follows.

Authentic: Narrated by Ahmad (8587), and al-Bukhari (2404) in suspended form.

5624 — Abu Hurairah narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: “There was a merchant who used to lend people money. Whenever he saw someone in hardship, he would say to his servants: ‘Overlook him, perhaps Allah will overlook us.’ So Allah overlooked him.”

٥٦٢٧ — عن حذيفة بن اليمان قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( تلقت الملائكة روح رجل ممن كان قبلكم، فقالوا: أعملت من الخير شيئا؟ قال: لا. قالوا: تذكر. قال: كنت أداين الناس، فآمر فتياني أن ينظروا المعسر، ويتجوزوا عن الموسر. قال: قال اللّٰه عز وجل: تجوزوا عنه )).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٠٧٧)، ومسلم (١٥٦٠)، واللفظ لمسلم.

وقوله: (( يتجوزوا )) من التجاوز، والتجوز معناه المسامحة في الاقتضاء والاستيفاء، وقبول ما فيه نقص.

english_source:
5627 — Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The angels received the soul of a man from those before you and said: ‘Did you do any good?’ He said: ‘No.’ They said: ‘Remember.’ He said: ‘I used to deal with people in debt, and I would order my young servants to give respite to the one in hardship and to be lenient with the one who had means.’ Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ‘Overlook him.’”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2077) and Muslim (1560). The wording is Muslim’s.

The phrase “be lenient” means to show forbearance in collecting and settling the debt, and to accept a lesser or easier return.

Then he found him, and the man said: “I am in hardship.” He said: “By Allah?” He said: “By Allah.” He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever would be pleased that Allah saves him from the distress of the Day of Resurrection, let him give respite to one in hardship or waive part of it for him.”

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1563).

٥٦٣٢ — عن بريدة بن الحصيب قال: سمعت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يقول: (( من أنظر معسرا فله كل يوم مثله صدقة )). قال: ثم سمعته يقول: (( من أنظر معسرا فله بكل يوم مثليه صدقة )). قلت: سمعتك يا رسول اللّٰه تقول: (( من أنظر معسرا فله بكل يوم مثله صدقة )). ثم سمعتك تقول: (( من أنظر معسرا فله بكل يوم مثليه صدقة )). قال: (( له بكل يوم صدقة قبل أن يحل الدين، فإذا حل الدين فأنظره فله بكل يوم مثليه صدقة )).

صحيح: رواه أحمد (٢٣٠٤٦) والحاكم (٢٩/٢)، واللفظ لأحمد.

english_source:
5632 — Buraydah ibn al-Husayb said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever gives respite to one in hardship will have the equivalent of it in charity each day.” Then I heard him say: “Whoever gives respite to one in hardship will have double its equivalent in charity each day.” I said: “I heard you, O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, say: ‘Whoever gives respite to one in hardship will have the equivalent of it in charity each day,’ then I heard you say: ‘Whoever gives respite to one in hardship will have double its equivalent in charity each day.’” He said: “He has charity for each day before the debt becomes due, and when the debt becomes due and he still grants respite, then he has double its equivalent in charity for each day.”

Authentic: Narrated by Ahmad (23046) and al-Hakim (2/29). The wording is Ahmad’s.

٥٦٣٣ — عن كعب بن مالك أنه تقاضى ابن أبي حَدرد دينا كان له عليه في المسجد، فارتفعت أصواتهما، حتى سمعها رسول اللّٰه ﷺ - وهو في بيته -، فخرج إليهما حتى كشف سجف حجرته، فنادى: (( يا كعب )). قال: لبيك يا رسول الله. قال: (( ضع من دينك هذا )). وأومأ إليه أي الشطر. قال: لقد فعلت يا رسول الله. قال: (( قم فاقضه )).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٥٧)، ومسلم (١٥٥٨).

english_source:
5633 — Kab ibn Malik was demanding from Ibn Abi Hadrad a debt owed to him in the mosque, and their voices rose until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard them while he was in his house. He came out to them and lifted the curtain of his room, then called out: “O Kab.” He said: “At your service, O Messenger of Allah ﷺ.” He said: “Reduce some of your debt,” and he indicated half of it. Kab said: “I have done so, O Messenger of Allah ﷺ.” He said: “Then stand and pay him.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (457) and Muslim (1558).

٥٦٣٤ — عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال:

أصيب رجل في عهد رسول الله ﷺ في ثمار ابتاعها، فكثر دينه، فقال رسول الله ﷺ:

«تَصَدَّقُوا عَلَيْهِ».

فتصدق الناس عليه، فلم يبلغ ذلك وفاء دينه.

فقال رسول الله ﷺ لغرمائه:

«خُذُوا مَا وَجَدْتُمْ، وَلَيْسَ لَكُمْ إِلَّا ذَلِكَ».

صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٥٥٦).

english_source:
5634 — Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī reported:

A man during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ suffered a loss in fruits that he had purchased, and his debts became numerous.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

“Give charity to him.”

The people gave charity to him, but what they gave was not enough to discharge his debt fully.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then said to his creditors:

“Take whatever you find, and you are entitled to nothing beyond that.”

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1556).

٥٦٣٥ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( من أدرك ماله بعينه عند رجل - أو إنسان - قد أفلس فهو أحق به من غيره )).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٤٠٢)، ومسلم (٢٢ :١٥٥٩).

ورواه مسلم (٢٤) من وجه آخر بلفظ: (( إذا أفلس الرجل فوجد الرجل متاعه بعينه فهو أحق به )). وفي رواية أخرى: (( فهو أحق به من الغرماء )).

english_source:
5635 — Abu Hurairah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever finds his property itself with a man — or a person — who has become bankrupt, he has more right to it than anyone else.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2402) and Muslim (1559:22).

Muslim also narrated it by another route with the wording: “If a man becomes bankrupt and another man finds his goods themselves, then he has more right to them.” In another wording: “then he has more right to it than the creditors.”

Muslim also narrated it by another route with the wording: “If a man becomes bankrupt and another man finds his goods themselves, then he has more right to them.” In another wording: “then he has more right to it than the creditors.”

٥٦٣٧ — عن أسيد بن ظهير الأنصاري أنه كان عاملا على اليمامة، وأن مروان كتب إليه أن معاوية كتب إلي: أيما رجل سرق منه سرقة فهو أحق بها حيث وجدها. قال: وكتب بذلك مروان إلي، فكتبت إلى مروان: أن النبي ﷺ قضى بأنه إذا كان الذي ابتاعها من الذي سرقها غير متهم يخير سيدها، فإن شاء أخذ الذي سرقت منه بثمنه، وإن شاء اتبع سارقه. ثم قضى بذلك بعد أبو بكر وعمر وعثمان. قال: فبعث مروان بكتابي إلى معاوية. قال: فكتب معاوية إلى مروان: إنك لست أنت ولا أسيد بن ظهير بقاضيين علي، ولكني أقضي فيما وليت عليكما، فأنفذ لما أمرتك به. فبعث مروان إلي كتاب معاوية، فقلت: لا أقضي به ما وليت، يعني بقول معاوية.

صحيح: أخرجه عبد الرزاق (١٧٩٨٦ ،١٨٨٢٩)، وأبو داود في المراسيل (١٨٠)، والنسائي (٤٦٨٠).

5637 — Usayd ibn Zuhayr al-Ansari was an official over al-Yamamah, and Marwan wrote to him that Muawiyah had written to him: Any man from whom something was stolen is more entitled to it wherever he finds it. He said: Marwan wrote that to me, so I wrote back to Marwan that the Prophet ﷺ had judged that if the one who bought it from the thief was not accused of wrongdoing, then its owner is given a choice: if he wishes, he takes back what was stolen from him and pays its price, and if he wishes, he may pursue the thief. Then Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman also judged by that. He said: Marwan sent my letter to Muawiyah. Muawiyah then wrote to Marwan: Neither you nor Usayd ibn Zuhayr are to judge over me; rather I judge in what I have authority over you, so carry out what I ordered you. Marwan sent me Muawiyah’s letter, and I said: I will not judge by it while I remain in authority — meaning by Muawiyah’s opinion.

Authentic: Related by Abd al-Razzaq (17986, 18829), Abu Dawud in al-Marasil (180), and al-Nasai (4680).

٥٦٣٨ — عن الشريد بن سويد الثقفي قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( لَيُّ الواجدِ يُحِلُّ عِرضَه وعقوبته )).

حسن: رواه أبو داود (٣٦٢٨)، والنسائي (٤٦٩٠ ،٤٦٨٩)، وابن ماجه (٢٤٢٧)، وأحمد (١٧٩٤٦).

وقوله: (( ليُّ الواجد )) بفتح اللام وتشديد الياء: التأخر. والواجد: القادر على أداء ما عليه من الدين.

وقوله: (( عرضه )) أي شكايته. وقوله: (( وعقوبته )) سجنه. قاله علي الطنافسي شيخ ابن ماجه.

5638 — Al-Sharid ibn Suwayd al-Thaqafi said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The delay of one who has means makes his honor lawful to speak against and makes punishment lawful.”

Hasan: Narrated by Abu Dawud (3628), al-Nasai (4689, 4690), Ibn Majah (2427), and Ahmad (17946).

The phrase “delay of one who has means” means postponement by a person able to repay his debt.

“His honor” means: complaint against him.

“And his punishment” means: imprisonment. This was explained by Ali al-Tanafisi, the teacher of Ibn Majah.

٥٦٣٩ — عن ابن أذنان قال: أسلفت علقمة ألفي درهم، فلما خرج عطاؤه قلت له: اقضني. قال: أخّرني إلى قابل، فأبيت عليه فأخذتها. قال: فأتيته بعدُ قال: برحتَ بي وقد منعتني. فقلت: نعم، هو عملك. قال: وما شأني؟ قلت: إنك حدثتني عن ابن مسعود أن النبي ﷺ قال: (( إن السلف يجري مجرى شطر الصدقة )). قال: نعم، فهو كذاك. قال: فخذ الآن.

حسن: رواه أحمد (٣٩١١) وأبو يعلى (٥٣٦٦)، وابن ماجه (٢٤٣٠).

5639 — Ibn Adhnan said: I lent Alqamah two thousand dirhams. When his stipend came out, I said to him: “Pay me.” He said: “Delay me until next year.” I insisted and took it. Later he said to me: “You pressed me hard and withheld ease from me.” I said: “Yes, that was your own doing.” He said: “What do you mean?” I said: “You narrated to me from Ibn Masud that the Prophet ﷺ said: ‘A loan runs in place of half of charity.’” He said: “Yes, that is so.” Then he said: “Take it now.”

Hasan: Narrated by Ahmad (3911), Abu Ya‘la (5366), and Ibn Majah (2430).

Later he said to me: “You pressed me hard and withheld ease from me.” I said: “Yes, that was your own doing.” He said: “What do you mean?” I said: “You narrated to me from Ibn Masud that the Prophet ﷺ said: ‘A loan runs in place of half of charity.’” He said: “Yes, that is so.” Then he said: “Take it now.”

Hasan: Narrated by Ahmad (3911), Abu Ya‘la (5366), and Ibn Majah (2430).

٥٦٤١ — عن عطية القرظي قال: عُرضنا على النبي ﷺ يوم قريظة، فكان من أنبت قتل، ومن لم ينبت خُلِّي سبيله، فكنت فيمن لم ينبت، فخُلِّي سبيلي.

صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٤٤٠٥)، والترمذي (١٥٨٤)، والنسائي (٤٩٨١)، وابن ماجه (٢٥٤١)، وأحمد (١٨٧٧٦). وقال الترمذي: “حسن صحيح”.

arabic_source:
٥٦٤٤ — عن عوف بن مالك بن الطفيل - وهو ابن الحارث، وهو ابن أخت عائشة زوج النبي ﷺ لأمها - أن عائشة حدَّثت أن عبد الله بن الزبير قال في بيع أو عطاء أعطته عائشة: والله لتنتهينَّ عائشة أو لأحجرنَّ عليها. فقالت: أهو قال هذا؟ قالوا: نعم. قالت: هو لله عليَّ نذر أن لا أكلم ابن الزبير أبداً. فاستشفع ابن الزبير إليها حين طالت الهجرة، فقالت: لا والله، لا أشفع فيه أبداً، ولا أتحنث إلى نذري. فلما طال ذلك على ابن الزبير كلَّم المسور بن مخرمة وعبد الرحمن بن الأسود بن عبد يغوث - وهما من بني زهرة -، وقال لهما: أنشدكما بالله لما أدخلتماني على عائشة؛ فإنها لا يحل لها أن تنذر قطيعتي. فأقبل به المسور وعبد الرحمن مشتملين بأرديتهما حتى استأذنا على عائشة، فقالا: السلام عليك ورحمة الله وبركاته، أندخل؟ قالت عائشة: ادخلوا. قالوا: كلنا؟ قالت: نعم، ادخلوا كلكم، ولا تعلم أن معهما ابن الزبير. فلما دخلوا دخل ابن الزبير الحجاب، فاعتنق عائشة، وطفق يناشدها، ويبكي، وطفق المسور وعبد الرحمن يناشدانها إلا ما كلمته، وقبلت منه، ويقولان: إن النبي ﷺ نهى عما قد علمتِ من الهجرة، فإنه لا يحل لمسلم أن يهجر أخاه فوق ثلاث ليال. فلما أكثروا على عائشة من التذكرة والتحريج طفقت تذكرهما، وتبكي، وتقول: إني نذرت، والنذر شديد. فلم يزالا بها حتى كلمت ابن الزبير، وأعتقت في نذرها ذلك أربعين رقبة، وكانت تذكر نذرها بعد ذلك، فتبكي حتى تبل دموعها خمارها.

صحيح: رواه البخاري (٦٠٧٣، ٦٠٧٤، ٦٠٧٥).

وهذا الحجر على عائشة لم يكن في محله؛ لأنها لم تكن سفيهة؛ فإن تصرفها كان صحيحاً، ولذا لم ترض بحجر ابن الزبير، بل شددت عليه بأن لا تكلمه أبداً.

english_source:
5644 — Awf ibn Malik ibn al-Tufayl — who was the son of al-Harith, and the son of the sister of Aishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ through her mother — narrated that Aishah said that Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr remarked concerning a sale or gift that Aishah had given: “By Allah, Aishah must stop, or I will place restrictions on her.” She said: “Did he really say this?” They said: Yes. She said: “Then for Allah upon me is a vow that I will never speak to Ibn al-Zubayr again.” Ibn al-Zubayr later sought intercession with her after the estrangement had become long, but she said: “No, by Allah, I will never intercede for him, nor will I break my vow.” When that became difficult for Ibn al-Zubayr, he asked al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad ibn Abd Yaghuth — both from Banu Zuhrah — and said to them: “I ask you by Allah to get me admitted to Aishah, for it is not lawful for her to vow to cut me off.” So al-Miswar and Abd al-Rahman came with him wrapped in their cloaks until they sought permission from Aishah. They said: “Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. May we enter?” Aishah said: “Enter.” They said: “All of us?” She said: “Yes, all of you may enter,” not realizing that Ibn al-Zubayr was with them. When they entered, Ibn al-Zubayr slipped behind the curtain, embraced Aishah, and began pleading with her and weeping. Al-Miswar and Abd al-Rahman also pleaded with her to speak to him and accept from him, saying: “The Prophet ﷺ forbade the kind of estrangement you already know. It is not lawful for a Muslim to abandon his brother for more than three nights.” When they repeatedly reminded and pressed her, she began recalling that and weeping, saying: “I made a vow, and a vow is serious.” They continued until she spoke to Ibn al-Zubayr, and she freed forty slaves as expiation for that vow. After that, whenever she remembered her vow, she would weep until her tears soaked her head covering.

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (6073, 6074, 6075).

This proposed restriction against Aishah was not appropriate, because she was not foolish in judgment. Her financial conduct was sound, and that is why she did not accept Ibn al-Zubayr’s attempt to restrict her, but instead became firm in refusing to speak to him.

٥٦٤٤ — عن عوف بن مالك بن الطفيل - وهو ابن الحارث، وهو ابن أخت عائشة زوج النبي ﷺ لأمها - أن عائشة حدَّثت أن عبد الله بن الزبير قال في بيع أو عطاء أعطته عائشة: والله لتنتهينَّ عائشة أو لأحجرنَّ عليها. فقالت: أهو قال هذا؟ قالوا: نعم. قالت: هو لله عليَّ نذر أن لا أكلم ابن الزبير أبداً. فاستشفع ابن الزبير إليها حين طالت الهجرة، فقالت: لا والله، لا أشفع فيه أبداً، ولا أتحنث إلى نذري. فلما طال ذلك على ابن الزبير كلَّم المسور بن مخرمة وعبد الرحمن بن الأسود بن عبد يغوث - وهما من بني زهرة -، وقال لهما: أنشدكما بالله لما أدخلتماني على عائشة؛ فإنها لا يحل لها أن تنذر قطيعتي. فأقبل به المسور وعبد الرحمن مشتملين بأرديتهما حتى استأذنا على عائشة، فقالا: السلام عليك ورحمة الله وبركاته، أندخل؟ قالت عائشة: ادخلوا. قالوا: كلنا؟ قالت: نعم، ادخلوا كلكم، ولا تعلم أن معهما ابن الزبير. فلما دخلوا دخل ابن الزبير الحجاب، فاعتنق عائشة، وطفق يناشدها، ويبكي، وطفق المسور وعبد الرحمن يناشدانها إلا ما كلمته، وقبلت منه، ويقولان: إن النبي ﷺ نهى عما قد علمتِ من الهجرة، فإنه لا يحل لمسلم أن يهجر أخاه فوق ثلاث ليال. فلما أكثروا على عائشة من التذكرة والتحريج طفقت تذكرهما، وتبكي، وتقول: إني نذرت، والنذر شديد. فلم يزالا بها حتى كلمت ابن الزبير، وأعتقت في نذرها ذلك أربعين رقبة، وكانت تذكر نذرها بعد ذلك، فتبكي حتى تبل دموعها خمارها.

صحيح: رواه البخاري (٦٠٧٣، ٦٠٧٤، ٦٠٧٥).

وهذا الحجر على عائشة لم يكن في محله؛ لأنها لم تكن سفيهة؛ فإن تصرفها كان صحيحاً، ولذا لم ترض بحجر ابن الزبير، بل شددت عليه بأن لا تكلمه أبداً.

5644 — Awf ibn Malik ibn al-Tufayl — who was the son of al-Harith, and the son of the sister of Aishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ through her mother — narrated that Aishah said that Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr remarked concerning a sale or gift that Aishah had given: “By Allah, Aishah must stop, or I will place restrictions on her.” She said: “Did he really say this?” They said: Yes. She said: “Then for Allah upon me is a vow that I will never speak to Ibn al-Zubayr again.” Ibn al-Zubayr later sought intercession with her after the estrangement had become long, but she said: “No, by Allah, I will never intercede for him, nor will I break my vow.” When that became difficult for Ibn al-Zubayr, he asked al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad ibn Abd Yaghuth — both from Banu Zuhrah — and said to them: “I ask you by Allah to get me admitted to Aishah, for it is not lawful for her to vow to cut me off.” So al-Miswar and Abd al-Rahman came with him wrapped in their cloaks until they sought permission from Aishah. They said: “Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. May we enter?” Aishah said: “Enter.” They said: “All of us?” She said: “Yes, all of you may enter,” not realizing that Ibn al-Zubayr was with them. When they entered, Ibn al-Zubayr slipped behind the curtain, embraced Aishah, and began pleading with her and weeping. Al-Miswar and Abd al-Rahman also pleaded with her to speak to him and accept from him, saying: “The Prophet ﷺ forbade the kind of estrangement you already know. It is not lawful for a Muslim to abandon his brother for more than three nights.” When they repeatedly reminded and pressed her, she began recalling that and weeping, saying: “I made a vow, and a vow is serious.” They continued until she spoke to Ibn al-Zubayr, and she freed forty slaves as expiation for that vow. After that, whenever she remembered her vow, she would weep until her tears soaked her head covering.

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (6073, 6074, 6075).

This proposed restriction against Aishah was not appropriate, because she was not foolish in judgment. Her financial conduct was sound, and that is why she did not accept Ibn al-Zubayr’s attempt to restrict her, but instead became firm in refusing to speak to him.

٥٦٤٥ — عن حنظلة يقول: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( لا يُتْمَ بعد احتلام، ولا يُتْمَ على جارية إذا هي حاضت )).

حسن: رواه الطبراني في الكبير (٤/١٦).

قال الخطابي: ظاهر هذا الحديث يوجب انقطاع أحكام اليتم عنه بالاحتلام، وحدوث أحكام البالغين له، فيكون للمحتلم أن يبيع ويشتري ويتصرف في ماله ويعقد النكاح لنفسه، وإن كانت امرأة فلا تزوج إلا بإذنها. ولكن المحتلم إذا لم يكن رشيداً لم يفك الحجر عنه، وقد يحظر الشيء بسببين، فلا يرتفع بارتفاع أحدهما مع بقاء السبب الآخر، وقد أمر اللّٰه تعالى بالحجر على السفيه، فقال: ( وَلَا تُؤْتُوا السُّفَهَاءَ أَمْوَالَكُمُ الَّتِي جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ قِيَامًا ) [سورة النساء: ٥].

5645 — Hanzalah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no orphanhood after puberty, and there is no orphanhood for a girl once she menstruates.”

Hasan: Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Kabir (4/16).

Al-Khattabi said: The apparent meaning of this hadith indicates that the rulings of orphanhood end upon puberty, and the rulings of adulthood begin. Thus, a person who has reached puberty may buy, sell, manage his wealth, and contract marriage for himself; and if it is a woman, she is not married off except with her permission. However, if the person who has reached puberty is not sound in judgment, then the restriction over him is not lifted. A thing may be restricted for two reasons, and it does not become unrestricted just because one reason is gone while the other remains. Allah the Exalted commanded restriction over the foolish person, saying: “Do not give the foolish your wealth which Allah has made a means of support for you.” [al-Nisa: 5]

5647 — Anas said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ pledged his armor for barley, and I went to the Prophet ﷺ with barley bread and stale melted fat. I heard him say: “The family of Muhammad ﷺ does not have as much as one sa of food in the morning nor in the evening, though they are nine households.”

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2508).

٥٦٤٨ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن عباس أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ مات ودرعه رهن عند يهودي بثلاثين صاعاً من شعير، أخذها رزقاً لعياله.

صحيح: رواه الترمذي (١٢١٤)، والنسائي (٤٦٥١)، وأحمد (٢١٠٩، ٣٤٠٩)، وقال: “حسن صحيح”.

وزاد أحمد في أول الحديث: أن النبي ﷺ التفت إلى أحد، فقال: (( والذي نفس محمد بيده، ما يسرني أن أحداً يحول لآل محمد ذهباً أنفقه في سبيل الله، أموت يوم أموت أدع منه دينارين إلا دينارين أعدهما لدين إن كان )). فمات وما ترك ديناراً ولا درهماً، ولا عبداً ولا وليدة، وترك درعه مرهونة عند يهودي … الحديث.

5648 — Abdullah ibn Abbas narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died while his armor was pledged with a Jew for thirty sa of barley, which he had taken as provision for his family.

Authentic: Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (1214), al-Nasai (4651), and Ahmad (2109, 3409). He said: “Hasan Sahih.”

Ahmad added at the beginning of the hadith that the Prophet ﷺ looked toward Uhud and said: “By the One in whose hand is Muhammad’s soul, it would not please me that the family of Muhammad had gold equal to Uhud which I spent in the path of Allah, then on the day I die I would leave behind from it two dinars — except two dinars set aside for a debt, if there were one.” So he died leaving behind neither dinar nor dirham, nor a male slave nor a female slave, and he left his armor pledged with a Jew … the hadith.

٥٦٤٩ — عن جابر قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( من لكعب بن الأشرف؛ فإنه قد آذى الله ورسوله ﷺ؟ )) قال محمد بن مسلمة: أنا. فأتاه، فقال: أردنا أن تسلفنا وسقاً أو وسقين. فقال: ارهنوني نساءكم. قالوا: كيف نرهنك نساءنا وأنت أجمل العرب؟ قال: فارهنوني أبناءكم. قالوا: كيف نرهنك أبناءنا فيسب أحدهم، فيقال: رهن بوسق أو وسقين، هذا عار علينا، ولكنا نرهنك اللأمة. قال سفيان: يعني السلاح. فوعده أن يأتيه، فقتلوه، ثم أتوا النبي ﷺ، فأخبروه.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٥١٠)، ومسلم (١٨٠١)، والسياق للبخاري.

5649 — Jabir said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Who will deal with Kab ibn al-Ashraf, for he has harmed Allah and His Messenger ﷺ?” Muhammad ibn Maslamah said: I will. He went to him and said: “We want you to lend us one or two wasqs.” He said: “Pledge your women to me.” They said: “How can we pledge our women to you when you are the most handsome of the Arabs?” He said: “Then pledge your sons to me.” They said: “How can we pledge our sons to you, and one of them would be insulted and it would be said that he was pledged for one or two wasqs? That would be a disgrace for us. But we can pledge you the la’mah.” Sufyan said: meaning weapons. So he promised to come to him, then they killed him, and afterward they came to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him.

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2510) and Muslim (1801). The wording here is al-Bukhari’s.

5650 — Abu Hurairah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “A pledged riding animal may be ridden in return for its maintenance if it has been pledged, and the milk of a pledged milking animal may be drunk in return for its maintenance if it has been pledged, and the one who rides and drinks must bear the maintenance.”

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2512).

٥٦٥١ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( لا يُغلق الرهن، له غنمه، وعليه غرمه )).

حسن: رواه الدارقطني (٣/٣٤).

وقوله: (( لا يُغلق الرهن )) معناه لا يستغلق بحيث لا يعود إلى الراهن، بل متى أدى الحق المرهون به عاد إلى الراهن.

وقوله: (( له غنمه )) أي الزوائد التي تحصل منه تكون للراهن.

وقوله: (( وعليه غرمه )) إذا هلك في يد المرتهن يكون من ضمان الراهن.

5651 — Abu Hurairah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “A pledge is not forfeited; its gain belongs to its owner, and its liability is upon him.”

Hasan: Narrated by al-Daraqutni (3/34).

The phrase “a pledge is not forfeited” means that it does not become permanently closed off so that it can never return to the pledger. Rather, whenever the debt for which it was pledged is paid, it returns to the pledger.

“its gain belongs to its owner” means that any increase or benefit arising from it belongs to the pledger.

“its liability is upon him” means that if it perishes while in the hand of the pledge-holder, its loss remains upon the pledger.

٥٦٥٣ — عن أبي موسى الأشعري قال: قال النبي ﷺ: (( إن الأشعريين إذا أرملوا في الغزو، أو قل طعام عيالهم بالمدينة جمعوا ما كان عندهم في ثوب واحد، ثم اقتسموه بينهم في إناء واحد بالسوية، فهم مني، وأنا منهم )).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٤٨٦)، ومسلم (٢٥٠٠).

english_source:
5653 — Abu Musa al-Ashari said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “When the Asharis become short of provisions during a campaign, or the food of their families in Madinah becomes scarce, they gather what they have into one cloth, then divide it equally among themselves in one vessel. They are from me, and I am from them.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2486) and Muslim (2500).

٥٦٥٤ — عن جبلة قال: كنا بالمدينة، فأصابتنا سنة، فكان ابن الزبير يرزقنا التمر، وكان ابن عمر يمر بنا، فيقول: لا تقرنوا؛ فإن النبي ﷺ نهى عن القِران إلا أن يستأذن الرجل منكم أخاه.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٤٨٩، ٢٤٩٠)، ومسلم (١٥٠ :٢٠٤٥)، والسياق للبخاري.

ورواه البخاري (٢٤٨٩) من طريق آخر بلفظ: “نهى النبي ﷺ أن يقرن الرجل بين التمرتين جميعاً حتى يستأذن أصحابه”.

english_source:
5654 — Jabalah said: We were in Madinah when a time of hardship struck us, and Ibn al-Zubayr used to provide us with dates. Ibn Umar would pass by us and say: “Do not combine two together, for the Prophet ﷺ forbade combining two dates together unless a man seeks permission from his companions.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2489, 2490) and Muslim (2045:150). The wording here is al-Bukhari’s.

Al-Bukhari also narrated by another route: “The Prophet ﷺ forbade a man from combining two dates together until he seeks permission from his companions.”

٥٦٥٥ — عن ابن عمر أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قال: (( من أعتق شركاً له في عبد، فكان له مال يبلغ ثمن العبد قُوِّم عليه قيمة العدل، فأعطى شركاءه حصصهم، وعتق عليه العبد، وإلا فقد عتق منه ما عتق )).

متفق عليه: رواه مالك (١)، والبخاري (٢٥٢٢)، ومسلم (١ :١٥٠١).

5655 — Ibn Umar narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever frees a share of his in a slave, and he has enough wealth to cover the price of the slave, the slave is fairly valued against him, then he gives his partners their shares, and the slave is fully freed on his behalf. Otherwise, only the portion that he freed is freed.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by Malik (1), al-Bukhari (2522), and Muslim (1501:1).

٥٦٥٦ — عن أبي هريرة عن النبي ﷺ قال: (( من أعتق شِقصاً من مملوكه فعليه خلاصه في ماله، فإن لم يكن له مال قوِّم المملوك قيمة عدل، ثم استسعي غير مشقوق عليه )).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٤٩٢)، ومسلم (١٥٠٣).

5656 — Abu Hurairah narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: “Whoever frees a share of his slave must complete his emancipation from his own wealth. If he does not have wealth, then the slave is fairly valued and then made to earn the remainder without being overburdened.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2492) and Muslim (1503).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٤٩٢)، ومسلم (١٥٠٣).

5656 — Abu Hurairah narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: “Whoever frees a share of his slave must complete his emancipation from his own wealth. If he does not have wealth, then the slave is fairly valued and then made to earn the remainder without being overburdened.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2492) and Muslim (1503).

٥٦٥٩ — عن أنس بن مالك:

أن أبا بكر رضي الله عنه كتب له فريضة الصدقة التي فرض رسول الله ﷺ، قال:

«وَمَا كَانَ مِنْ خَلِيطَيْنِ فَإِنَّهُمَا يَتَرَاجَعَانِ بَيْنَهُمَا بِالسَّوِيَّةِ».

صحيح: رواه البخاري (٢٤٨٧).

Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote for him the ordinance of zakat prescribed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. It stated:

“Whatever belongs to two partners whose livestock are mixed together, they shall settle between themselves equally.”

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (2487).

٥٦٦٠ — عن جابر بن عبد اللّٰه قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( من كان له شريك في ربعة أو نخل فليس له أن يبيع حتى يؤذن شريكه، فإن رضي أخذ، وإن كره ترك )).

صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٣٣ :١٦٠٨).

ولفظ ابن جريج: (( قضى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ بالشفعة في كل شركة لم تقسم ربعة أو حائط، لا يحل له أن يبيع حتى يؤذن شريكه، فإن شاء أخذ، وإن شاء ترك، فإذا باع ولم يؤذنه فهو أحق به )).

english_source:
5660 — Jabir ibn Abdullah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever has a partner in a dwelling or in date-palms, it is not lawful for him to sell until he informs his partner. If the partner is pleased, he takes it, and if he dislikes it, he leaves it.”

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1608:133).

In the wording of Ibn Jurayj: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled with preemption in every undivided partnership in a house or a garden. It is not lawful for him to sell until he informs his partner. If he wishes, he takes it, and if he wishes, he leaves it. If he sells without informing him, then the partner has more right to it.”

Hasan: Narrated by Ahmad (16994).

٥٦٦٢ — عن النعمان بن بشير قال: سمعت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يقول - وأهوى النعمان بإصبعيه إلى أذنيه -: (( إن الحلال بيّن، وإن الحرام بيّن، وبينهما مشتبهات لا يعلمهن كثير من الناس، فمن اتقى الشبهات استبرأ لدينه وعرضه، ومن وقع فى الشبهات وقع فى الحرام، كالراعي يرعى حول الحمى يوشك أن يرتع فيه. ألا وإن لكل ملك حمى، ألا وإن حمى اللّٰه محارمه، ألا وإن فى الجسد مضغة إذا صلحت صلح الجسد كله، وإذا فسدت فسد الجسد كله، ألا وهي القلب )).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٠٥١)، ومسلم (١٥٩٩/١٠٧)، واللفظ لمسلم.

english_source:
5662 — Al-Nu‘man ibn Bashir said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say — and al-Nu‘man pointed with his two fingers to his ears —: “The lawful is clear, and the unlawful is clear, and between them are doubtful matters that many people do not know. Whoever avoids the doubtful matters has protected his religion and his honor. Whoever falls into doubtful matters falls into the unlawful, like a shepherd grazing around a protected boundary, soon to graze within it. Indeed, every king has a protected boundary, and indeed the protected boundary of Allah is His prohibitions. Indeed, in the body there is a morsel of flesh: if it is sound, the whole body is sound; and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Truly, it is the heart.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2051) and Muslim (1599/107). The wording is Muslim’s.

٥٦٦٢ — عن النعمان بن بشير قال: سمعت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يقول - وأهوى النعمان بإصبعيه إلى أذنيه -: (( إن الحلال بيّن، وإن الحرام بيّن، وبينهما مشتبهات لا يعلمهن كثير من الناس، فمن اتقى الشبهات استبرأ لدينه وعرضه، ومن وقع فى الشبهات وقع فى الحرام، كالراعي يرعى حول الحمى يوشك أن يرتع فيه. ألا وإن لكل ملك حمى، ألا وإن حمى اللّٰه محارمه، ألا وإن فى الجسد مضغة إذا صلحت صلح الجسد كله، وإذا فسدت فسد الجسد كله، ألا وهي القلب )).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٠٥١)، ومسلم (١٥٩٩/١٠٧)، واللفظ لمسلم.

5662 — Al-Nu‘man ibn Bashir said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say — and al-Nu‘man pointed with his two fingers to his ears —: “The lawful is clear, and the unlawful is clear, and between them are doubtful matters that many people do not know. Whoever avoids the doubtful matters has protected his religion and his honor. Whoever falls into doubtful matters falls into the unlawful, like a shepherd grazing around a protected boundary, soon to graze within it. Indeed, every king has a protected boundary, and indeed the protected boundary of Allah is His prohibitions. Indeed, in the body there is a morsel of flesh: if it is sound, the whole body is sound; and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Truly, it is the heart.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2051) and Muslim (1599/107). The wording is Muslim’s.

٥٦٦٥ — عن جابر بن عبد الله:

أن رسول الله ﷺ وأصحابه مروا بامرأة، فذبحت لهم شاة، واتخذت لهم طعامًا.

فلما رجع قالت:

يا رسول الله، إنا اتخذنا لكم طعامًا، فادخلوا فكلوا.

فدخل رسول الله ﷺ وأصحابه، وكانوا لا يبدؤون حتى يبتدئ النبي ﷺ.

فأخذ النبي ﷺ لقمة فلم يستطع أن يسيغها، فقال النبي ﷺ:

«هَذِهِ شَاةٌ ذُبِحَتْ بِغَيْرِ إِذْنِ أَهْلِهَا».

فقالت المرأة:

يا نبي الله، إنا لا نحتشم من آل سعد بن معاذ، ولا يحتشمون منا، نأخذ منهم ويأخذون منا.

صحيح: رواه أحمد (١٤٧٨٥)، والحاكم (٤/٢٣٤-٢٣٥).

5665 — Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh reported:

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions passed by a woman. She slaughtered a sheep for them and prepared food.

When they returned, she said:

“O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, we have prepared food for you, so come in and eat.”

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions entered. They would not begin eating until the Prophet ﷺ began.

The Prophet ﷺ took a morsel but was unable to swallow it. He said:

“This sheep was slaughtered without the permission of its owners.”

The woman said:

“O Prophet of Allah, there is no formality between us and the family of Saʿd ibn Muʿādh, nor between them and us. We take from them, and they take from us.”

Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (14785) and al-Ḥākim (4/234–235).

٥٦٦٦ — عن رجلٍ من الأنصار أخبره قال: خرجنا مع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ في جنازة، فلما رجعنا لقينا داعي امرأة من قريش، فقال: يا رسول اللّٰه، إن فلانة تدعوك ومن معك إلى طعام. فانصرف ﷺ، وانصرفنا معه، فجلسنا مجالس الغلمان من آبائهم بين أيديهم، ثم جيء بالطعام، فوضع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يده، ووضع القوم أيديهم، ففطن له القوم، وهو يلوك لقمته لا يجيزها، فرفعوا أيديهم، وغفلوا عنا، ثم ذكروا فأخذوا بأيدينا، فجعل الرجل يضرب اللقمة بيده حتى تسقط، ثم أمسكوا بأيدينا ينظرون ما يصنع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فلفظها فألقاها، فقال: (( أجد لحم شاة أُخذت بغير إذن أهلها )). فقامت المرأة فقالت: يا رسول اللّٰه، إنه كان في نفسي أن أجمعك ومن معك على طعام، فأرسلت إلى البقيع فلم أجد شاة تباع، وكان عامر بن أبي وقاص ابتاع شاة أمس من البقيع، فأرسلت إليه أن ابتع لي شاة من البقيع فلم توجد، فذكر لي أنك اشتريت شاة فأرسل بها إليَّ، فلم يجدْه الرسول، ووجد أهله، فدفعوها إلى رسولي، فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( أطعموها الأسارى )).

حسن: رواه أبو داود (٣٣٣٢)، وأحمد (٢٢٥٠٩)، والسياق لأحمد.

5666 — A man from the Ansar reported: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in a funeral procession. When we returned, the messenger of a woman from Quraysh met us and said: “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so-and-so invites you and those with you to a meal.” So he turned aside, and we turned aside with him. We sat as children sit before their fathers. Then the food was brought. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ placed his hand in it, and the people also put their hands in it. Then the people noticed that he was chewing his morsel without being able to swallow it. So they withdrew their hands, though they forgot about us at first, then remembered and took our hands back. The man began knocking the morsel from his hand until it fell, and they kept holding our hands, watching what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would do. Then he spat it out and said: “I find this to be the meat of a sheep taken without the permission of its owners.” The woman then stood and said: “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I wished to gather you and those with you for a meal, so I sent to al-Baqi, but I did not find a sheep for sale. Amir ibn Abi Waqqas had bought a sheep yesterday from al-Baqi, so I sent to him that he should buy one for me from al-Baqi, but none was found. Then I was told that you had bought a sheep, so I sent for it, but the messenger did not find him; he found his family, and they handed it to my messenger.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Feed it to the prisoners.”

Hasan: Narrated by Abu Dawud (3332) and Ahmad (22509). This wording is Ahmad’s.

٥٦٦٦ — عن رجلٍ من الأنصار أخبره قال: خرجنا مع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ في جنازة، فلما رجعنا لقينا داعي امرأة من قريش، فقال: يا رسول اللّٰه، إن فلانة تدعوك ومن معك إلى طعام. فانصرف ﷺ، وانصرفنا معه، فجلسنا مجالس الغلمان من آبائهم بين أيديهم، ثم جيء بالطعام، فوضع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يده، ووضع القوم أيديهم، ففطن له القوم، وهو يلوك لقمته لا يجيزها، فرفعوا أيديهم، وغفلوا عنا، ثم ذكروا فأخذوا بأيدينا، فجعل الرجل يضرب اللقمة بيده حتى تسقط، ثم أمسكوا بأيدينا ينظرون ما يصنع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فلفظها فألقاها، فقال: (( أجد لحم شاة أُخذت بغير إذن أهلها )). فقامت المرأة فقالت: يا رسول اللّٰه، إنه كان في نفسي أن أجمعك ومن معك على طعام، فأرسلت إلى البقيع فلم أجد شاة تباع، وكان عامر بن أبي وقاص ابتاع شاة أمس من البقيع، فأرسلت إليه أن ابتع لي شاة من البقيع فلم توجد، فذكر لي أنك اشتريت شاة فأرسل بها إليَّ، فلم يجدْه الرسول، ووجد أهله، فدفعوها إلى رسولي، فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( أطعموها الأسارى )).

حسن: رواه أبو داود (٣٣٣٢)، وأحمد (٢٢٥٠٩)، والسياق لأحمد.

5666 — A man from the Ansar reported: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in a funeral procession. When we returned, the messenger of a woman from Quraysh met us and said: “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so-and-so invites you and those with you to a meal.” So he turned aside, and we turned aside with him. We sat as children sit before their fathers. Then the food was brought. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ placed his hand in it, and the people also put their hands in it. Then the people noticed that he was chewing his morsel without being able to swallow it. So they withdrew their hands, though they forgot about us at first, then remembered and took our hands back. The man began knocking the morsel from his hand until it fell, and they kept holding our hands, watching what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would do. Then he spat it out and said: “I find this to be the meat of a sheep taken without the permission of its owners.” The woman then stood and said: “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I wished to gather you and those with you for a meal, so I sent to al-Baqi, but I did not find a sheep for sale. Amir ibn Abi Waqqas had bought a sheep yesterday from al-Baqi, so I sent to him that he should buy one for me from al-Baqi, but none was found. Then I was told that you had bought a sheep, so I sent for it, but the messenger did not find him; he found his family, and they handed it to my messenger.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Feed it to the prisoners.”

Hasan: Narrated by Abu Dawud (3332) and Ahmad (22509). This wording is Ahmad’s.

٥٦٦٧ — عن كاتب المغيرة بن شعبة قال: كتب معاوية إلى المغيرة بن شعبة أن اكتب إليَّ بشيء سمعته من النبي ﷺ، فكتب إليه: سمعت النبي ﷺ يقول: (( إن اللّٰه كره لكم ثلاثاً: قيل وقال، وإضاعة المال، وكثرة السؤال )).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٤٧٧)، ومسلم (٥٩٣/١٣).

وفي رواية: (( إن اللّٰه حرم ثلاثاً، ونهى عن ثلاث: حرم عقوق الوالدين، ووأد البنات، ولا وهات. ونهى عن ثلاث: قيل وقال، وكثرة السؤال، وإضاعة المال )). وفي رواية: (( ومنعاً وهات )).

وقوله: (( ولا وهات )) أي حرم قول: لا، يعني الامتناع عن أداء ما تجب عليه من الحقوق، ويقول فيما ليس له فيه حق: أعط.

5667 — The scribe of al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah said: Muawiyah wrote to al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah: “Write to me something you heard from the Prophet ﷺ.” So he wrote to him: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “Allah dislikes for you three things: gossiping back and forth, wasting wealth, and asking too much.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (1477) and Muslim (593/13).

In another wording: “Allah has made three things unlawful and forbidden three things: He made unlawful disobedience to parents, burying daughters alive, and saying ‘don’t give’ while demanding ‘give me.’ And He forbade three things: gossiping back and forth, excessive questioning, and wasting wealth.” In another wording: “withholding and demanding.”

The phrase means refusing to give what one is obliged to give, while demanding what one has no right to demand.

٥٦٦٨ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( إن اللّه يرضى لكم ثلاثاً، ويكره لكم ثلاثاً، فيرضى لكم أن تعبدوه، ولا تشركوا به شيئاً، وأن تعتصموا بحبل اللّٰه جميعاً، ولا تفرقوا. ويكره لكم قيل وقال، وكثرة السؤال، وإضاعة المال )).

صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٧١٥).

5668 — Abu Hurairah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Allah is pleased for you with three things and dislikes for you three things. He is pleased that you worship Him and associate nothing with Him, that you hold firmly together to the rope of Allah and do not become divided. And He dislikes for you gossiping back and forth, asking too much, and wasting wealth.”

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1715).

5670 — Abu Hurairah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by a heap of food and put his hand into it. His fingers touched dampness, so he said: “What is this, O owner of the food?” He said: “Rain fell on it, O Messenger of Allah ﷺ.” He said: “Why did you not put it on top of the food so people could see it? Whoever deceives is not from me.”

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (102).

Ahmad (7292) and Abu Dawud (3492) also narrated it, and in one wording: he was inspired to put his hand into it, and when he found it wet, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “He is not from us who deceives.”

Hasan: Narrated by Ibn Majah (2246), al-Hakim (2/8), and al-Bayhaqi (5/320).

٥٦٧٥ — عن أبي هريرة قال: سمعت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يقول: (( الحلف منفقة للسلعة، ممحقة للبركة )).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٠٨٧)، ومسلم (١٦٠٦)، واللفظ للبخاري.

قوله: (( منفقة )) بفتح الميم والفاء، بينهما نون ساكنة، من النفاق، وهو الرواج ضد الكساد.

5675 — Abu Hurairah said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Swearing may make the goods sell, but it wipes out the blessing.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2087) and Muslim (1606). The wording is al-Bukhari’s.

The word means that it causes the goods to move and sell, the opposite of stagnation.

٥٦٧٦ — عن أبي هريرة يقول: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( ثلاثة لا ينظر اللّٰه إليهم يوم القيامة ولا يزكيهم ولهم عذاب أليم: رجل كان له فضل ماء بالطريق فمنعه من ابن السبيل، ورجل بايع إماماً لا يبايعه إلا لدنيا، فإن أعطاه منها رضي، وإن لم يعطه منها سخط، ورجل أقام سلعته بعد العصر، فقال: واللّه الذي لا إله غيره لقد أُعطيت بها كذا وكذا فصدقه رجل )) ثم قرأ هذه الآية: ( إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَشْتَرُونَ بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ وَأَيْمَٰنِهِمْ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا ) [آل عمران: ٧٧].

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٣٥٨)، ومسلم (١٠٨).

english_source:
5676 — Abu Hurairah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There are three whom Allah will not look at on the Day of Resurrection, nor purify them, and they will have a painful punishment: a man who has excess water on the road but withholds it from a traveler; a man who gives allegiance to a leader only for worldly gain — if he is given something from it he is pleased, and if he is not given he is angered; and a man who displays his goods after the Asr prayer and says: ‘By Allah, besides whom there is no god, I was offered such-and-such for it,’ and a man believes him.” Then he recited the verse: “Indeed, those who trade away the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price…” [Al Imran: 77]

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2358) and Muslim (108).

5676 — Abu Hurairah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There are three whom Allah will not look at on the Day of Resurrection, nor purify them, and they will have a painful punishment: a man who has excess water on the road but withholds it from a traveler; a man who gives allegiance to a leader only for worldly gain — if he is given something from it he is pleased, and if he is not given he is angered; and a man who displays his goods after the Asr prayer and says: ‘By Allah, besides whom there is no god, I was offered such-and-such for it,’ and a man believes him.” Then he recited the verse: “Indeed, those who trade away the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price…” [Al Imran: 77]

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2358) and Muslim (108).

٥٦٧٨ — عن أبي ذر، عن النبي ﷺ قال: (( ثلاثة لا يكلمهم اللّٰه يوم القيامة ولا ينظر إليهم ولا يزكيهم ولهم عذاب أليم )). قال: فقرأها رسول اللٰه ﷺ ثلاث مرار. قال أبو ذر: خابوا وخسروا، من هم يا رسول الله؟ قال: (( المسبل، والمنان، والمنفق سلعته بالحلف الكاذب )).

صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٠٦).

وفي رواية: (( والمنفق سلعته بالحلف الفاجر، والمسبل إزاره )).

والمنفِّق بالتشديد من النفاق، وهو ضد الكساد.

5678 — Abu Dharr narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: “There are three whom Allah will not speak to on the Day of Resurrection, nor look at, nor purify, and they will have a painful punishment.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ repeated it three times. Abu Dharr said: “They are ruined and lost — who are they, O Messenger of Allah ﷺ?” He said: “The one who lets his garment hang below his ankles, the one who reminds others of his favors, and the one who sells his goods by false oaths.”

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (106).

In another wording: “the one who promotes his goods by wicked oaths, and the one who lets his garment hang low.”

Here it means the one who makes his goods sell and circulate, the opposite of goods remaining unsold.

٥٦٧٩ — عن مطرف بن عبد اللّٰه بن الشخير قال: بلغني عن أبي ذر حديث، فكنت أحب أن ألقاه، فلقيته، فقلت له: يا أبا ذر، بلغني عنك حديث، فكنت أحب أن ألقاك فأسألك عنه. فقال: قد لقيت فاسأل. قال: قلت: بلغني أنك تقول: سمعت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يقول: (( ثلاثة يحبهم الله، وثلاثة يبغضهم اللّه )). قال: نعم، فما إخالك أكذب على خليلي محمد ﷺ - ثلاثاً يقولها - قال: قلت: من الثلاثة الذين يحبهم اللّٰه عز وجل؟ قال: (( رجل غزا في سبيل الله، فلقي العدو مجاهداً محتسباً، فقاتل حتى قتل، وأنتم تجدون في كتاب اللّٰه عز وجل: ( إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُقَاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِهِ صَفًّا ) [الصف: ٤]، ورجل له جار يؤذيه، فيصبر على أذاه ويحتسبه حتى يكفيه الله إياه بموت أو حياة، ورجل يكون مع قوم فيسيرون حتى يشق عليهم الكرى أو النعاس، فينزلون في آخر الليل، فيقوم إلى وضوئه وصلاته )).

قال: قلت: من الثلاثة الذين يبغضهم اللّٰه؟ قال: (( الفخور المختال، وأنتم تجدون في كتاب اللّٰه عز وجل: ( إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ مُخْتَالٍ فَخُورٍ ) [لقمان: ١٨]، والبخيل المنان، والتاجر - أو البياع - الحلاف )). قال: قلت: يا أبا ذر، ما المال؟ قال: فِرَقٌ لنا وذودٌ - يعني غنماً يسيرة -. قال: قلت: لست عن هذا أسأل، إنما أسألك عن صامت المال. قال: ما أصبح لا أمسى، وما أمسى لا أصبح. قال: قلت: يا أبا ذر، ما لك ولإخوتك قريش؟ قال: والله لا أسألهم دنيا، ولا أستفتيهم عن دين اللّٰه حتى ألقى اللّٰه ورسوله. ثلاثاً يقولها.

صحيح: رواه أحمد (٢١٥٣٠)، والطبراني في الكبير (٢/١٦١)، والحاكم (٢/٨٨-٨٩)، واللفظ لأحمد.

5679 — Mutarrif ibn Abdullah ibn al-Shikhkhir said: A hadith from Abu Dharr reached me, and I wished to meet him. When I met him, I said: “O Abu Dharr, a hadith from you reached me, and I wanted to meet you to ask you about it.” He said: “You have met me, so ask.” I said: “I heard that you say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say, ‘Three are loved by Allah, and three are hated by Allah.’” He said: “Yes, and I do not think I would lie about my beloved Muhammad ﷺ” — repeating that three times. I said: “Who are the three whom Allah loves?” He said: “A man who goes out fighting in the way of Allah, meets the enemy striving and seeking reward, and fights until he is killed — and you find in the Book of Allah: ‘Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in ranks’ [al-Saff: 4]; a man who has a neighbor who harms him, yet he remains patient over his harm seeking reward until Allah relieves him of him, whether by death or by life; and a man who is traveling with people until drowsiness and sleep become hard on them, so they camp at the end of the night, and he gets up for his ablution and prayer.”

I said: “Who are the three whom Allah hates?” He said: “The boastful arrogant one — and you find in the Book of Allah: ‘Indeed, Allah does not love every self-deluded boaster’ [Luqman: 18] — the stingy one who reminds others of his favors, and the trader — or seller — who swears frequently.”

I said: “O Abu Dharr, what is wealth?” He said: “A small flock and a few camels for us,” meaning a little livestock. I said: “That is not what I mean; I mean stored wealth.” He said: “What is with me in the morning does not remain till evening, and what is with me in the evening does not remain till morning.” I said: “O Abu Dharr, what is there between you and your brothers from Quraysh?” He said: “By Allah, I do not ask them for worldly things, nor do I seek legal opinions from them in the religion of Allah until I meet Allah and His Messenger.” He said that three times.

Authentic: Narrated by Ahmad (21530), al-Tabarani in al-Kabir (2/161), and al-Hakim (2/88–89). The wording is Ahmad’s.

I said: “Who are the three whom Allah loves?” He said: “A man who goes out fighting in the way of Allah, meets the enemy striving and seeking reward, and fights until he is killed — and you find in the Book of Allah: ‘Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in ranks’ [al-Saff: 4]; a man who has a neighbor who harms him, yet he remains patient over his harm seeking reward until Allah relieves him of him, whether by death or by life; and a man who is traveling with people until drowsiness and sleep become hard on them, so they camp at the end of the night, and he gets up for his ablution and prayer.”

I said: “Who are the three whom Allah hates?” He said: “The boastful arrogant one — and you find in the Book of Allah: ‘Indeed, Allah does not love every self-deluded boaster’ [Luqman: 18] — the stingy one who reminds others of his favors, and the trader — or seller — who swears frequently.”

I said: “O Abu Dharr, what is wealth?” He said: “A small flock and a few camels for us,” meaning a little livestock. I said: “That is not what I mean; I mean stored wealth.” He said: “What is with me in the morning does not remain till evening, and what is with me in the evening does not remain till morning.” I said: “O Abu Dharr, what is there between you and your brothers from Quraysh?” He said: “By Allah, I do not ask them for worldly things, nor do I seek legal opinions from them in the religion of Allah until I meet Allah and His Messenger.” He said that three times.

٥٦٧٩ — عن مطرف بن عبد اللّٰه بن الشخير قال: بلغني عن أبي ذر حديث، فكنت أحب أن ألقاه، فلقيته، فقلت له: يا أبا ذر، بلغني عنك حديث، فكنت أحب أن ألقاك فأسألك عنه. فقال: قد لقيت فاسأل. قال: قلت: بلغني أنك تقول: سمعت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يقول: (( ثلاثة يحبهم الله، وثلاثة يبغضهم اللّه )). قال: نعم، فما إخالك أكذب على خليلي محمد ﷺ - ثلاثاً يقولها - قال: قلت: من الثلاثة الذين يحبهم اللّٰه عز وجل؟ قال: (( رجل غزا في سبيل الله، فلقي العدو مجاهداً محتسباً، فقاتل حتى قتل، وأنتم تجدون في كتاب اللّٰه عز وجل: ( إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُقَاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِهِ صَفًّا ) [الصف: ٤]، ورجل له جار يؤذيه، فيصبر على أذاه ويحتسبه حتى يكفيه الله إياه بموت أو حياة، ورجل يكون مع قوم فيسيرون حتى يشق عليهم الكرى أو النعاس، فينزلون في آخر الليل، فيقوم إلى وضوئه وصلاته )).

قال: قلت: من الثلاثة الذين يبغضهم اللّٰه؟ قال: (( الفخور المختال، وأنتم تجدون في كتاب اللّٰه عز وجل: ( إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ مُخْتَالٍ فَخُورٍ ) [لقمان: ١٨]، والبخيل المنان، والتاجر - أو البياع - الحلاف )). قال: قلت: يا أبا ذر، ما المال؟ قال: فِرَقٌ لنا وذودٌ - يعني غنماً يسيرة -. قال: قلت: لست عن هذا أسأل، إنما أسألك عن صامت المال. قال: ما أصبح لا أمسى، وما أمسى لا أصبح. قال: قلت: يا أبا ذر، ما لك ولإخوتك قريش؟ قال: والله لا أسألهم دنيا، ولا أستفتيهم عن دين اللّٰه حتى ألقى اللّٰه ورسوله. ثلاثاً يقولها.

صحيح: رواه أحمد (٢١٥٣٠)، والطبراني في الكبير (٢/١٦١)، والحاكم (٢/٨٨-٨٩)، واللفظ لأحمد.

٥٦٨٠ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن أبي أوفى أن رجلاً أقام سلعة وهو في السوق، فحلف بالله لقد أُعطي بها ما لم يُعط؛ ليوقع فيها رجلاً من المسلمين، فنزلت: ( إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَشْتَرُونَ بِعَهْدِ ٱللَّهِ وَأَيْمَٰنِهِمْ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا ) [آل عمران: ٧٧].

صحيح: رواه البخاري (٢٠٨٨).

english_source:
5680 — Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa said: A man displayed goods in the market and swore by Allah that he had been offered for them what he had not actually been offered, intending to deceive a Muslim into buying them. Then the verse was revealed: “Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price…” [Al Imran: 77]

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2088).

٥٦٨١ — عن أبي قتادة الأنصاري:

أنه سمع رسول الله ﷺ يقول:

«إِيَّاكُمْ وَكَثْرَةَ الْحَلِفِ فِي الْبَيْعِ؛ فَإِنَّهُ يُنَفِّقُ، ثُمَّ يَمْحَقُ».

صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٦٠٧).

5681 — Abū Qatādah al-Anṣārī reported that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

“Beware of excessive swearing in transactions, for it may make the merchandise sell, but afterward it erases the blessing.”

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1607).

٥٦٨٢ — عن عبد الرحمن بن شبل قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( إنَّ التُّجَّارَ هُمُ الفُجَّارُ )). قيل: يا رسولَ اللّٰه، أوَليس قد أحلَّ اللّٰه البيعَ؟ قال: (( بلى، ولكنهم يُحدِّثون فيكذبون، ويَحلفون فيأثمون )).

صحيح: رواه أحمد (١٥٥٣٠)، والحاكم (٧-٦/٢)، والبيهقي في شعب الإيمان (٢١٨/٤).

5682 — Abd al-Rahman ibn Shibl reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Merchants are the sinful ones.” It was said: “Messenger of Allah ﷺ, has Allah not made trade lawful?” He said: “Yes, but they speak and lie, and they swear oaths and thereby sin.”

Authentic: Narrated by Ahmad (15530), al-Hakim (2/6–7), and al-Bayhaqi in Shu‘ab al-Iman (4/218).

Authentic: Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu‘jam al-Kabir (6/301).

٥٦٨٤ — عن أبي سعيد قال: مرَّ أعرابيٌّ بشاة، فقلتُ: تبيعنيها بثلاثة دراهم؟ قال: لا واللّٰه، ثم باعنيها، فذكرتُ ذلك لرسول اللّٰه ﷺ فقال: (( باع آخرتَه بدُنياه )).

5684 — Abu Sa‘id reported: A desert Arab passed by with a sheep, and I said, “Will you sell it to me for three dirhams?” He said, “No, by Allah,” then he sold it to me. I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: “He sold his Hereafter for his worldly gain.”

Hasan: Narrated by Ibn Hibban (4909).

٥٦٨٤ — عن أبي سعيد قال: مرَّ أعرابيٌّ بشاة، فقلتُ: تبيعنيها بثلاثة دراهم؟ قال: لا واللّٰه، ثم باعنيها، فذكرتُ ذلك لرسول اللّٰه ﷺ فقال: (( باع آخرتَه بدُنياه )).

حسن: رواه ابن حبان (٤٩٠٩).

5684 — Abu Sa‘id reported: A desert Arab passed by with a sheep, and I said, “Will you sell it to me for three dirhams?” He said, “No, by Allah,” then he sold it to me. I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: “He sold his Hereafter for his worldly gain.”

Hasan: Narrated by Ibn Hibban (4909).

٥٦٨٥ — عن قيس بن أبي غَرَزَة قال: كنّا في عهد رسول اللّٰه ﷺ نُسمَّى السماسرة، فمرَّ بنا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فسمّانا باسمٍ هو أحسن، فقال: (( يا معشرَ التُّجّارِ، إنَّ البيعَ يحضره اللغوُ والحلفُ، فشوبوه بالصدقة )).

صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٣٣٢٦)، والترمذي (١٢٠٨)، والنسائي (٣٧٩٧)، وابن ماجه (٢١٤٥)، وأحمد (١٦١٣٤).

وقوله: (( كنّا نُسمَّى السماسرة )) جمع سمسار، وهو اسمٌ للتاجر الوسيط. وقوله: (( فشوبوه بالصدقة )) أي اخلطوا تجارتكم بالصدقة لتكفِّر ما قد يقع فيها من اللغو والحلف ونحو ذلك.

٥٦٨٦ — عن البراء بن عازب قال: قال: أتانا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ إلى البقيع، فقال: (( يا معشرَ التُّجّارِ ))، حتى إذا أشرأبُّوا قال: (( إنَّ التُّجّارَ يُحشرون يوم القيامة فُجّارًا إلا من اتّقى وبرَّ وصدق )).

حسن: رواه البيهقي في شعب الإيمان (٤٥٠٧).

english_source:
5686 — Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib reported: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us at al-Baqi‘ and said: “O merchants.” When they raised their heads to listen, he said: “Merchants will be raised on the Day of Resurrection as sinful people, except those who fear Allah, act righteously, and speak truthfully.”

Hasan: Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Shu‘ab al-Iman (4507).

٥٦٨٧ — عن عطاء بن يسار قال: لقيتُ عبدَ اللّٰه بن عمرو بن العاص، قلتُ: أخبرني عن صفة رسول اللّٰه ﷺ في التوراة. قال: أجل، واللّٰه، إنّه لموصوفٌ في التوراة ببعض صفته في القرآن: {يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ شَاهِدًا وَمُبَشِّرًا وَنَذِيرًا} [الأحزاب: ٤٥]، وحرزًا للأميين، أنت عبدي ورسولي، سمّيتُك المتوكّل، ليس بفظٍّ ولا غليظٍ ولا سخّابٍ في الأسواق، ولا يدفع بالسيئة السيئة، ولكن يعفو ويغفر، ولن يقبضه اللّٰه حتى يقيم به الملّة العوجاء بأن يقولوا: لا إله إلا اللّٰه، ويفتح بها أعينًا عميًا، وآذانًا صمًّا، وقلوبًا غلفًا.

صحيح: رواه البخاري (٢١٢٥).

english_source:
5687 — ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar said: I met Abdullah ibn ‘Amr ibn al-‘As and said, “Tell me about the description of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the Torah.” He said: “Yes, by Allah, he is described in the Torah with some of the description found in the Quran: ‘O Prophet, We have sent you as a witness, a bringer of good news, and a warner.’ He is a protection for the unlettered people. You are My servant and My messenger. I have named you the Reliant One. He is neither harsh nor hard-hearted nor loud and quarrelsome in the marketplaces. He does not repay evil with evil, but rather pardons and forgives. Allah will not take him until He straightens through him the crooked religion, so that they say: There is no god but Allah, and through him He opens blind eyes, deaf ears, and sealed hearts.”

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2125).

٥٦٨٨ — عن عمرو بن شعيب، عن أبيه، عن جدّه أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ نهى عن الشراء والبيع في المسجد، وأن تُنشد فيه ضالّة، وأن يُنشد فيه شعر، ونهى عن التحلّق قبل الصلاة يوم الجمعة.

5688 — ‘Amr ibn Shu‘ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade buying and selling in the mosque, announcing lost property in it, reciting poetry in it, and sitting in circles before the Friday prayer.

Hasan: Narrated by Abu Dawud (1079), al-Tirmidhi (322), al-Nasa’i (716), and authenticated by Ibn Khuzaymah (1306).

full_display_content:
٥٦٨٨ — عن عمرو بن شعيب، عن أبيه، عن جدّه أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ نهى عن الشراء والبيع في المسجد، وأن تُنشد فيه ضالّة، وأن يُنشد فيه شعر، ونهى عن التحلّق قبل الصلاة يوم الجمعة.

حسن: رواه أبو داود (١٠٧٩)، والترمذي (٣٢٢)، والنسائي (٧١٦)، وصححه ابن خزيمة (١٣٠٦).

٥٦٩٠ — عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي ﷺ قال: (( اجتنبوا السبع الموبقات )). قالوا: يا رسول اللّٰه، وما هن؟ قال: (( الشرك باللّٰه، والسحر، وقتل النفس التي حرّم اللّٰه إلا بالحق، وأكل الربا، وأكل مال اليتيم، والتولّي يوم الزحف، وقذف المحصنات المؤمنات الغافلات )).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٧٦٦)، ومسلم (٨٩).

english_source:
5690 — Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet said: “Avoid the seven destructive sins.” They said: “Messenger of Allah ﷺ, what are they?” He said: “Associating partners with Allah, sorcery, killing a soul that Allah has forbidden except with right, consuming usury, consuming the property of an orphan, fleeing on the day of battle, and accusing chaste, believing, unsuspecting women.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2766) and Muslim (89).
